## Purpose and selected system

Extract capacitance/conductance and AC resistance/inductance matrices for the
finite-ground CPW coupon. Preserve its finite Signal, two Ground conductors
and substrate rather than substituting an infinite line section.
C/G and AC/RL are distinct extraction products, not full-wave S-parameters.

## Model, boundaries and current paths

Use the notebook's body geometry, material records, conductor thickness and
physical Z. Preserve the surrounding region and its exterior/reference
treatment. State matrix ordering, units and any reference reduction.

Bind each body to its intended Signal or Ground Net. C/G describes the
electric conductor arrangement; AC/RL additionally needs the authored current
path. Specify the Signal source and sink objects and their face directions.
Ground classification is not a source/sink assignment.

Extraction frequency selects the material/current response under study.
Mesh and adaptive pass settings govern numerical extraction. Exact values,
enabled matrix families and output selections live in the notebook.

::: {.callout-note}
A superconducting material identity must retain the actual native modeling
interpretation. It does not by itself prove an extracted kinetic inductance.
:::

## Workflow

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Palace

For a static capacitance question, use the separately defined
[electrostatic workflow](electrostatic-capacitance.qmd). A Palace comparison
must state its reference and boundary conventions; it is not a substitute
for this current-path-dependent AC/RL extraction.

### AEDT

Use [Finite CPW Q3D](../../notebooks/ComponentSimulation/CpwFiniteGround/aedt_q3d.ipynb).
Construct the native bodies, inspect material and Net assignments, bind the
source/sink pair and extract the requested families. Analyze returned matrices
separately from preparation.

:::

## Expected outputs

Retain native body/material and Net readback, source/sink faces and directions,
applied setup and adaptive history. Return C/G and AC/RL outputs with their
actual frequencies, units and conductor ordering. Keep any reduced matrix or
derived circuit quantity linked to its raw matrix and convention.

Do not label capacitance-only output as completed AC/RL extraction, or
interpret a matrix entry without its reference/current-path definition.
No new extraction accuracy or agreement threshold is introduced here.

See [source ownership](../tools/source-ownership.qmd),
